fr:mainmatter.html:p: In Slow Chains of Fillers for Reindexings for Instantiating Vertical Exponentials, we mention an intractable slowness when instantiating vertical universal properties in the dislayed category of sets. There is a similar slowness when shoing that this displayed category is a fibration. Our first proof attempt uses reind-filler,
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: funExt₂ λ z zᴰ → Xᴰ.Prectify {e' = refl {x = f (g z)}} $ Xᴰ.≡out $ (sym $ Xᴰ.reind-filler λ i → f (g (transp (λ j → fst Z) i z))) ∙ (sym $ Xᴰ.reind-filler _) -- can't really fill this argument because the resulting term has an hcomp with unfilled arguments ∙ Xᴰ.cong₂ᴰ γᴰ ((sym $ Zᴰ.reind-filler λ i → transp (λ j → fst Z) (~ i) (transp (λ j → fst Z) i0 z)) ∙ (sym $ Zᴰ.reind-filler λ i → transp (λ j → fst Z) (~ i) z)) where module Xᴰ = hSetReasoning X (λ x → ⟨ Xᴰ x ⟩) module Zᴰ = hSetReasoning Z (λ z → ⟨ Zᴰ z ⟩)
fr:mainmatter.html:p: Typechecking the above takes between 5 and 10 seconds. But we can upgrade it to typecheck nearly instantaneously by replacing it with manual usage of hcomp.
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: λ j → transp (λ _ → (x : fst Z) → fst (Zᴰ x) → fst (Xᴰ (f (g x)))) j (transp (λ i → (x : fst Z) → fst (Zᴰ x) → fst (Xᴰ (hcomp (λ k → λ { (i = i0) → f (g x) ; (i = i1) → f (g x) ; (j = i1) → f (g x) }) (hcomp (λ k → λ { (~ i = i0) → f (g x) ; (~ i = i1) → f (g x) ; (j = i1) → f (g x) }) (f (g x)))))) j (λ x p → γᴰ x p))
fr:mainmatter.html:p: I suspect that the reason that this is faster relates to the semantics as cubes. My hypothesis is that the chain of reind-fillers is describing a high-dimensional cube by walking the edges of it one at a time, whereas the faster version that explicitly mentions and hcomp directly specifies the cube all at once. In this manner, there is no coherence overhead in verifying that the arguments to the reinds (which are just opaque substs) are what they are expect to be. That is, I expect there to be a better strategy for proving equalities that look like chains of transport (or subst or reind) by instead specifying the cube en masse.
